'Is holm-keyed to' is symmetric..why: A made-up relation (holm_keyed_to, fictional, no property tags before the insert) given a property and applied to real instances. The name "holm-keyed" is not a mathematical term, so a model has no default reading of it with this property, and an unrecorded relation has no property to contradict. Paired with mathematics-replace-0010.

notes: RBox expansion, symmetry, paired with mathematics-replace-0010 (which makes 'is a multiple of' symmetric). The made-up relation 'is holm-keyed to' relates different whole numbers; 'keyed to' has a direction (a key opens a lock) and no built-in mutuality, unlike 'linked', 'paired' or 'matched', so a model has no default reading of it as symmetric. The instance pairs (9 and 40, 33 and 7) share no divisor or size pattern. Every original answer is null. Yes and no are balanced through phrasing: the direct question and the first instance ask whether the converse could fail (no; the first instance is 'Could 40 fail to be holm-keyed to 9?', not whether the pair rules it out, since that 'no' holds without the edit), the second instance whether it follows (yes); the cross-lingual queries ask the first instance. As in other symmetry inserts, a symmetric edit has no honest 'no' instance, so the pre-edit audit should record the base models' yes rate. The propositional negation is worded 'Is it true that ... is not symmetric?'. Side facts (triangle) are copied from the paired revision. Near unrelated asks symmetry of 'is less than', a real relation whose answer is no; a leak would turn it to yes. hops counts the instance fact in the prompt as the bridge (1 + 1).
